title: Inspect nations' laws and religions; the Jewish people and Moses; Christian religion true or none is
pass_a_gloss: First the constitutions and laws of kingdoms are to be inspected. Second the religions of all nations — none which cannot be convicted absurd from reason itself. Whatever right reason openly teaches to be false is false also in theology. Third one must approach the Jewish people, most ancient. Fourth from the writings of Moses it is to be demonstrated how God revealed himself. Fifth that the things Christians teach are founded in Moses is to be proved, in the manner of Grotius, Justin Martyr, Ficino, Mornay. Sixth: Either the Christian religion, of which sacred scripture is the principle, is the true religion, or there is no true religion in the world. But that there is none is false from providence. Therefore the Christian religion is the true religion.
pass_b_english: First, inspect kingdoms' laws, whose only end is fleeting earthly good. Second, inspect all nations' religions: though they promise eternal life, none escapes being shown absurd from reason itself. Whatever right reason plainly teaches false is false also in theology — the same thing cannot be true and false at once.

Third, come to the Jewish people, whom even pagans acknowledge as most ancient, and whose Moses leaves Greek historical memory behind. Fourth, from Moses demonstrate how God revealed Himself and the way to eternal life. Fifth, prove that what Christians teach is founded in Moses — as Grotius, Justin Martyr, Ficino, and Mornay did. Sixth, argue: Either the Christian religion, whose principle is Sacred Scripture, is the true religion, or there is no true religion in the world. But it is false that there is none (from providence, nn. 5–6). Therefore the Christian religion is the true religion.
source_text: Inspiciendae leges gentium & religiones (omnes absurdae praeter Christianam); populus Judaicus & Moses; Christiani in Mose fundati (Grotius, Justinus, Ficinus, Mornaeus). Aut religio Christiana, cujus sacra scriptura principium est, vera est religio, aut nulla est in orbe vera religio. Atqui falsum est nullam esse… Ergo Christiana vera.
